summary.intent: Assess whether GSD Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability) needed discussion before planning, clean up drifted todos across Phases 70/70.1/71/72/73, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 end-to-end before repeating the same flow for Phase 73.
summary.outcome: Discovered and fixed three unrelated CI regressions from Phases 70.1/71 (web-e2e floor store, FUSE seq-1 equivocation, sdk-e2e Test 21 flake) plus four additional local web-e2e timing flakes, merged PRs #600 and #601, then fully planned and executed all 10 Phase 72 plans (SC#1-#6) on main, including an unplanned but user-directed test-file TypeScript drift cleanup (113 errors, vitest v2→v3 + Phase-62 type retirement) and wiring a build-first test-inclusive typecheck into CI; phase verification/shipping was still in progress (resolving stale skipped tests) when the transcript ends.

repo: GSD repo closes todos by deleting/moving files from pending/ to completed/, not by leaving markers — Phase 71 shipped (#599) without retiring its 8 source todos, causing pending/ drift

ci-e2e.yml (Web/Desktop E2E) only triggers on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on older workflow definitions) to validate before merging

tests/web-e2e uses ciFloor() to raise wait timeouts to 60s only under CI env; local runs use much tighter timeouts (15-30s), causing IPNS-gated ops (deletes, mkdirs, restores) to reliably flake locally even though they pass in CI — representative local verification requires CI=1 plus temporarily patching webServer.reuseExistingServer (which is `!process.env.CI`)

packages/sdk and packages/sdk-core resolve @cipherbox/* cross-package imports via workspace-symlinked dist output, not path aliases/project references — test-inclusive typecheck must run after build, per package in dependency order (crypto→core→api-client→sdk-core→sdk)

Only tsconfig.build.json excludes test files; the base tsconfig.json includes them, but no package had a `typecheck` script and root `pnpm typecheck` only ran builds — so CI never typechecked test files, letting 113 errors accumulate (vitest v2→v3 Mock generics drift + Phase-62 retired type usage in tests)

sdk-e2e Test 21 (D-06 concurrent first-publish) is inherently non-deterministic post-Phase-71: same-CID/same-seq concurrent publishes can legitimately return either two 200s (idempotent) or one 200+one 409 (insert-race) — asserting exactly one 409 is a flake, not a bug
desktop-e2e workflow dispatch always runs both web AND desktop jobs together — can't validate one in isolation via dispatch
Commits sometimes appear to hang/timeout locally due to 1Password SSH signing prompts, but usually land anyway — verify with git log/status rather than assuming failure

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty' — a stale/dropped UploadComplete retry would re-seal at seq=1 with a new CID, tripping Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate; fixed by resolving IPNS first and routing 'Found' outcomes into the existing CAS bump path via publish_with_cas_retry, later optimized with an optional preresolved_seq param to avoid a redundant second resolve

getWriteBodyParams (and its twin in bin/index.ts) fail-open on a transient IPNS resolve miss, silently sealing an empty write-body and discarding the folder's write chain; SC#2 fix makes it throw when a real (non-zero, 32-byte) writeKey is present and resolve genuinely returns null, while preserving the legitimate zero-writeKey read-only fallback

readDurableFloors/writeDurableSeqFloor still probed retired IndexedDB stores generation-high-water/seq-high-water; Phase 70.1 collapsed them into a single rotation-floor store keyed by nodeId (DB cipherbox-rotation-state v2) — helper needed to be repointed, not the product code

walkChildWriteKey(mode) dedup: unseal/AEAD-tamper failures must always propagate (throw), never collapse to null — only the missing-WriteChildRef case should be mode-gated between nullable and fail-closed behavior, otherwise consolidating call sites turns a fail-closed tamper-detection path into fail-open

workflow: When a background subagent's fix needs live sdk-e2e/CI validation but the executor sandbox can't read .env, defer that validation to the orchestrator/wave-gate level rather than blocking the plan

Route source fixes through the same PR that surfaced the flake when the fix is orthogonal but small (e.g. sdk-e2e Test 21 fix landed on #600 instead of a new branch) — fewer PRs, and the fix's own CI run becomes its validation

When a systemic pattern emerges from flaky tests, apply targeted source fixes only if the user prefers preserving strict philosophy (e.g. retries:0) rather than reaching for blanket retry/timeout config changes

Capture emergent, user-directed scope expansions (like 'fix all TS drift, wire CI') as a durable todo file immediately, then sequence it as a final phase plan rather than doing it ad hoc mid-wave, so it also covers files not yet created
Rebase a stacked PR onto main after a sibling PR merges (even with no file overlap) before dispatching validation workflows, so the dispatched run reflects true post-merge integration state
git stash is usable to preserve uncommitted cross-cutting bookkeeping (todo moves + ROADMAP edits) across an unrelated branch detour (CI firefighting) without committing prematurely

friction: Wasted several review cycles peeking wrong todo directory (resolved/ vs completed/) before user corrected
gh workflow run -f ref= returned HTTP 422 because the workflow definition on main predated that input; had to discover --ref <branch> as the working alternative

Six consecutive local web-e2e runs cascaded on different flaky tests one at a time (4.10→4.11→2.1→2.1 again) before the root cause was recognized as a systemic local/CI timeout asymmetry (ciFloor only applies under CI)

CI=1 locally flips webServer.reuseExistingServer to false, refusing to reuse the already-running dev stack — required a temporary, reverted playwright.config.ts patch to get a representative CI-equivalent local run
Hooks/config JSON for GSD plan:pre gates contained raw control characters in string values, breaking both `--raw` output and standard JSON.parse; required writing a custom lenient parser script

Full test-file TypeScript inventory (113 errors) turned out to be two different problems disguised as one (vitest v2→v3 Mock generics in sdk-core/api-client vs. Phase-62 retired-type fallout in sdk tests), requiring re-scoping mid-task

Sequential background-agent commits produced git-status/cat-file inconsistencies that needed a second, more decisive check to resolve (false negative on whether completed/ todo copies were actually in HEAD)
